pages.quiz:
AGRICULTURE — MOCK EXAM #4
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: AGRICULTURE
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. About how long does compost usually take to be ready? (1 mark)
   A. Two years
   B. One day
   C. Two to three months
   D. Ten minutes

2. What could a school use to make a simple drip system? (1 mark)
   A. A plastic bottle with tiny holes in the cap
   B. A wooden door
   C. A stone
   D. A broom

3. Which is a problem of cutting many trees for firewood? (1 mark)
   A. More rain falls at once
   B. Forests shrink and soil can be washed away
   C. The soil becomes richer
   D. Trees grow faster

4. What does it mean to conserve fuel? (1 mark)
   A. To hide it
   B. To use only what is needed and make it last
   C. To burn as much as possible
   D. To waste it

5. What is a wild animal? (1 mark)
   A. An animal kept in a house
   B. An animal sold in shops
   C. An animal that lives freely in nature
   D. An animal kept for milk

6. Why is it wrong to kill every bird that visits a field? (1 mark)
   A. Birds pay tax
   B. Birds cannot eat crops
   C. Birds also eat harmful insects and are part of nature
   D. Birds are always good

7. Why do we use more than one method of scaring animals? (1 mark)
   A. It uses more soil
   B. One method is always cheaper
   C. Animals can get used to one method
   D. It confuses farmers

8. Which crop is likely to be eaten by birds? (1 mark)
   A. Firewood
   B. Rocks
   C. Ripening millet
   D. Compost

9. What is thinning? (1 mark)
   A. Removing extra seedlings so the rest have room
   B. Adding more seeds
   C. Cutting all plants
   D. Making soil thin

10. Why do we cover the seeds with a thin layer of fine soil? (1 mark)
   A. To let birds find them
   B. To make them bigger
   C. To stop them growing
   D. To protect them and keep them moist

11. When should fruits be harvested? (1 mark)
   A. When they are ripe
   B. Before flowers appear
   C. While green and hard
   D. After they rot

12. Which of these fruits grows on a woody tree? (1 mark)
   A. Passion fruit
   B. Grapes
   C. Blackberry
   D. Mango

13. Which of these is a climbing fruit crop? (1 mark)
   A. Orange
   B. Guava
   C. Passion fruit
   D. Mango

14. Which of these is a benefit of growing your own fruit? (1 mark)
   A. Fresh fruit for the family at low cost
   B. Fewer vitamins
   C. More expenses
   D. Less food

15. Which site is suitable for planting a fruit tree? (1 mark)
   A. A flooded area
   B. A deep shade under big trees
   C. Inside a building
   D. A sunny place with space to spread

16. What is the purpose of vaccinating animals? (1 mark)
   A. To colour them
   B. To make them heavier
   C. To make them noisy
   D. To prevent diseases

17. How does manure from animals help crops? (1 mark)
   A. It scares birds
   B. It gives shade
   C. It supplies plant food to the soil
   D. It makes crops small

18. What is a domestic animal? (1 mark)
   A. An animal that lives freely in the forest
   B. An animal found only in parks
   C. An animal kept and cared for by people
   D. An animal that cannot be tamed

19. Why is it a good idea to use the water from boiled vegetables in soup? (1 mark)
   A. It has no use
   B. It is dirty
   C. It contains vitamins that came out of the vegetables
   D. It is poisonous

20. Which of these is used for boiling food? (1 mark)
   A. A plate
   B. A saucepan with a lid
   C. A basket
   D. A frying pan only

21. Which way should pot handles point? (1 mark)
   A. Towards children
   B. Down into the fire
   C. Inward, away from the edge
   D. Outward over the floor

22. How should drinking water be stored? (1 mark)
   A. On the ground
   B. In an open basin
   C. In a clean container with a lid
   D. With a dirty cup

23. Which is a method of cleaning the home? (1 mark)
   A. Planting
   B. Sowing
   C. Mopping
   D. Grafting

24. Why should stagnant water be emptied from tins and tyres? (1 mark)
   A. It cools the compound
   B. It smells of soap
   C. Mosquitoes lay eggs in it
   D. It is too clean

25. How should broken glass be disposed of? (1 mark)
   A. Left on the floor
   B. Wrapped in thick paper and given to an adult
   C. Thrown in the yard
   D. Put in the compost

26. Which PPE is worn on the feet at school and in the garden? (1 mark)
   A. Dust mask
   B. Gloves
   C. Overall
   D. Canvas shoes

27. What should you do if your PPE is damaged? (1 mark)
   A. Tell a teacher or an adult
   B. Keep using it
   C. Throw it in a river
   D. Hide it

28. Why should cleaning be done in an open place with drainage? (1 mark)
   A. To be seen
   B. To make noise
   C. So dirty water does not make a puddle
   D. To get wet

29. Which is a mistake in tacking? (1 mark)
   A. Marking the line first
   B. Using contrasting thread
   C. Making stitches of different lengths in even tacking
   D. Using small back stitch at the end

30. When is even tacking most useful? (1 mark)
   A. Only for paper
   B. For curves and slippery cloth
   C. When you do not want to sew
   D. Only for straight seams that need no hold

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Compare a watering can with drip irrigation. (4 marks)

32. Give three signs that fruit is ripe, naming the fruit. (3 marks)

33. Give three benefits of eating a balanced meal. (3 marks)

34. Give three reasons why a clean home is important. (3 marks)

35. Explain why vegetables and fruits should be eaten every day. (3 marks)

36. Explain what is meant by a balanced meal. (2 marks)

37. State two safety rules when making a scarecrow. (2 marks)

38. Explain what thinning is and why it is done. (3 marks)

39. Describe how to keep a food journal for one week. (4 marks)

40. Describe how to clean gumboots. (4 marks)

41. Name four fuels used for cooking in homes. (2 marks)

42. Give three reasons why fruits are important. (3 marks)

43. Give three ways of saving fuel when cooking. (3 marks)

44. Describe how to make a simple trellis for passion fruit. (4 marks)

45. Describe how to clean canvas shoes. (4 marks)

46. Give three uses of chickens. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
AGRICULTURE — MOCK EXAM #4 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — Two to three months
   It depends on weather and materials but is usually two to three months.

2. A — A plastic bottle with tiny holes in the cap
   A bottle with small holes in its cap drips slowly.

3. B — Forests shrink and soil can be washed away
   Trees protect soil and water, so cutting them harms the environment.

4. B — To use only what is needed and make it last
   Conserving fuel means saving it.

5. C — An animal that lives freely in nature
   Wild animals are not kept by people.

6. C — Birds also eat harmful insects and are part of nature
   Wild animals are needed for balance in nature.

7. C — Animals can get used to one method
   A mix of methods works better.

8. C — Ripening millet
   Birds eat ripening grain such as millet and sorghum.

9. A — Removing extra seedlings so the rest have room
   Thinning gives strong plants space.

10. D — To protect them and keep them moist
   Covering helps seeds germinate.

11. A — When they are ripe
   Ripe fruit is tastiest and has the most vitamins.

12. D — Mango
   Mango grows on a woody tree.

13. C — Passion fruit
   Passion fruit needs support to climb.

14. A — Fresh fruit for the family at low cost
   Growing at home saves money.

15. D — A sunny place with space to spread
   Fruit trees need light and space.

16. D — To prevent diseases
   Vaccination protects animals from diseases.

17. C — It supplies plant food to the soil
   Manure enriches the soil.

18. C — An animal kept and cared for by people
   Domestic animals depend on people for food, water and shelter.

19. C — It contains vitamins that came out of the vegetables
   Some vitamins go into the cooking water.

20. B — A saucepan with a lid
   A saucepan holds water.

21. C — Inward, away from the edge
   Handles sticking out can be knocked.

22. C — In a clean container with a lid
   Covering keeps germs out.

23. C — Mopping
   Mopping cleans floors.

24. C — Mosquitoes lay eggs in it
   Mosquitoes spread malaria.

25. B — Wrapped in thick paper and given to an adult
   This prevents cuts.

26. D — Canvas shoes
   Canvas shoes protect feet.

27. A — Tell a teacher or an adult
   Damaged PPE may not protect you.

28. C — So dirty water does not make a puddle
   Dirty water can breed mosquitoes.

29. C — Making stitches of different lengths in even tacking
   Stitches should be equal.

30. B — For curves and slippery cloth
   Even tacking holds firmly.

SECTION B
----
31. (4 marks)
   Answer: A watering can wets a wide area and much water is lost by running off and by evaporation. Drip irrigation puts water beside the roots slowly, so less is used, fewer weeds grow, and the leaves stay dry.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for the watering can, 2 marks for drip irrigation.

32. (3 marks)
   Answer: Passion fruit turns purple or yellow and wrinkles; guava turns yellowish and smells sweet; pawpaw turns yellow or orange and gives when pressed.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each sign with fruit.

33. (3 marks)
   Answer: It gives energy, helps the body to grow and repair, and protects from illness.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each benefit.

34. (3 marks)
   Answer: It prevents diseases, keeps food safe, prevents accidents and looks pleasant.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

35. (3 marks)
   Answer: They give vitamins and minerals, fibre for digestion and water, so they protect the body from disease.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point.

36. (2 marks)
   Answer: A meal that has foods from all the main food groups in the right amounts.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for foods from all groups, 1 mark for right amounts.

37. (2 marks)
   Answer: Ask an adult to help with sharp or heavy work; do not use wire or broken glass; wear gloves for rough poles (any two).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each rule.

38. (3 marks)
   Answer: It is removing extra seedlings. It gives the remaining plants space and reduces competition for water, light and food.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for meaning, 2 marks for reasons.

39. (4 marks)
   Answer: Draw a table; write what you eat at every meal; write the group of each food; at the end of the week check which groups were missing.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

40. (4 marks)
   Answer: Knock off lumps of mud; rinse; scrub with a soft brush and soapy water inside and outside; rinse again; dry upside down in the shade.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four steps.

41. (2 marks)
   Answer: Firewood, charcoal, gas and kerosene.
   Working / marking points: Half a mark for each fuel, total 2.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: They give vitamins, they give fibre and water, and they can be sold for money.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: Use a lid on the pot, cut food small, use dry firewood, put out the fire after cooking, soak beans first, or use an improved jiko (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each way.

44. (4 marks)
   Answer: Fix strong posts about 2 m tall; tie strong wires or strings between them; plant seedlings near the posts; tie the stems gently to the wires.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct step.

45. (4 marks)
   Answer: Remove laces; brush off loose dirt; scrub gently with soapy water; rinse; stuff with paper; dry in the shade.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four steps.

46. (3 marks)
   Answer: Eggs, meat, manure, feathers and income (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each use.
